blocks.x: Harlem could be one step closer to a major subway upgrade, with the MTA moving forward on plans for a new crosstown tunnel beneath 125th Street.
The proposed extension would connect multiple subway lines and Metro-North Railroad, making it easier to travel across Manhattan without relying on crowded buses or transferring downtown.

The project is still in its early stages, but a new environmental review is underway, and reusing equipment from the Second Avenue Subway could save taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars and more than two years of construction time.
Which Subway Lines Would the 125th Street Extension Connect To?

Currently under construction, Phase 2 of the Second Avenue Subway (SAS) will extend the Q train to 125th Street & Lexington Avenue. The two massive tunnel boring machines (TBMs) utilized for Phase 2 will complete their run under West 125th Street between Lenox Avenue and Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard. The MTA’s plan aims to keep these machines digging westward to carve out a new crosstown tunnel shell across Upper Manhattan.
Lenox Avenue: Transfer to the 2 and 3 trains.
St. Nicholas Avenue: Transfer to the A, C, B, and D trains.
Broadway: Transfer to the 1 train.
Lexington Avenue & Metro-North: Direct connection to the 4, 5, 6, and Q trains alongside the Metro-North Railroad Harlem-125th Street Station.

Source / MTA
The Project Could Make Crosstown Travel Across Harlem Much Easier
125th Street is Manhattan’s busiest crosstown bus corridor, where passengers frequently encounter heavy traffic delays.

Direct East-West Transit: Harlemites would gain a fast, one-seat ride across Harlem and direct connections to jobs, healthcare, and educational institutions on both the East and West Sides of Manhattan.

Ridership & Traffic Impact: MTA estimates project over 164,000 daily riders using the corridor, attracting roughly 5,500 new daily transit riders while eliminating over 21,600 vehicle miles traveled daily on city streets.
Reusing Second Avenue Subway Equipment Could Save Millions

By keeping the Phase 2 Tunnel Boring Machines (TBMs) moving westward instead of dismantling, extracting, and re-mobilizing heavy equipment years later, the project captures substantial efficiency savings:
Cost Savings: Reusing active TBMs and existing site setup is estimated to save taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars.
Accelerated Timeline: Seamlessly continuing excavation shaves more than two years off the overall tunneling construction schedule.

Legislative Support: Governor Kathy Hochul’s FY 2026 budget secured initial feasibility funding and enacted a State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) amendment that permits preliminary design and engineering to proceed alongside the environmental review.

Shutterstock / Here Now
When Could the 125th Street Subway Extension Become a Reality?
The project is progressing through initial environmental and design milestones:
Fall 2026: Public scoping period and community input sessions open.
Early 2027 (Q1 / Winter): Expected release of the Draft Environmental Impact Statement (EIS).

Future Phasing: The current environmental review specifically covers civil tunnel construction. Laying tracks, installing signal systems, building stations, and introducing passenger train service will be designed, funded, and reviewed in subsequent project phases.
How New Yorkers Can Weigh In on the Proposed Subway Project
The MTA is accepting public input on the draft scope of work through November 13, 2026. Community members can participate through multiple channels:
Public Comment Sessions
Virtual Sessions (via Zoom): Thursday, October 22, 2026 | 12:00 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m.
In-Person Session: Tuesday, October 27, 2026 | 5:30 p.m. – 8:00 p.m. at the Adam Clayton Powell, Jr. State Office Building (2nd Floor Community Room, 163 W 125th St, New York, NY 10027)
Submitting Written Comments
Online: Submit comments directly at mta.info/project/125-street-subway.
Email: Send feedback directly to 125StSubwayTunnel@mtacd.org.

Mail: Address written correspondence to:
MTA Government & Community Relations
Attn: 125 Street Subway
2 Broadway, D16.94
New York, NY 10004
For more information, see the project’s official homepage.
